title: The One Idea Per Slide Rule (blog explainer)

brief.motion: Confident editorial motion graphics: one big idea at a time, soft depth and glow, springy pops that land on the spoken word, slow camera drift, crisp slide-split mechanics that show a crowded slide breaking into clean single-idea slides.
brief.story: A crowded slide becomes four clear ones. Dark violet stage with a coral accent. The single glowing idea is the recurring motif: one thing in focus, everything else dimmed.

scenes.narration: If a slide needs two headlines, it's two slides. Here's why one idea per slide is the most useful rule in presentation design.

slide.title: One idea per slide
slide.notes: If a slide needs two headlines, it's two slides. Here's why one idea per slide is the most useful rule in presentation design.

scenes.storyboard: dark violet stage. A single slide card floats in with a glow. Two headlines try to sit on it, on 'two headlines' a hairline splits the card into two cards that slide apart with a springy pop. The title 'One idea per slide' typesets large over the top as the cards settle.

beats.text: If a slide needs two headlines, it's two slides.
Here's why one idea per slide is the most useful rule in presentation design.

scenes.narration: Here's a typical crowded slide. A vague headline, and four separate ideas fighting for attention. Split it, and each point gets its own headline.

slide.title: Q3 update
slide.text: Revenue up on last quarter. Two new enterprise customers signed. Churn rose in the small-business segment. Hiring two more account managers
slide.notes: Here's a typical crowded slide. A vague headline, and four separate ideas fighting for attention. Split it, and each point gets its own headline.

scenes.storyboard: a cluttered slide card titled 'Q3 update' with four bullet rows; the rows feel cramped and a faint noisy shimmer shows the clutter. On 'split it' the card shatters cleanly along the row lines into four fresh cards that fan out in a row, each with a bold single-sentence headline: 'Revenue grew again in Q3', 'Two enterprise customers signed', 'Small-business churn is rising', 'Hiring two account managers'. Land each new headline as the narrator says 'own headline'.

beats.text: A vague headline, and four separate ideas fighting for attention.
Split it, and each point gets its own headline.

scenes.narration: The audience knows where to look. What they see stays in step with what they hear. And in a video, every new idea means a fresh picture on screen.

slide.title: Why the rule works
slide.text: The audience knows where to look. What they see matches what they hear. It works better as video. Easier to update
slide.notes: The audience knows where to look. What they see stays in step with what they hear. And in a video, every new idea means a fresh picture on screen.

scenes.storyboard: three glowing icon-orbs build in a row, one per phrase: an eye / focus ring on 'where to look', an ear plus eye linked by a pulsing line on 'in step with what they hear', then a film strip whose frames flip through different pictures on 'fresh picture'. Each orb lights up on its phrase while the others dim.

beats.text: The audience knows where to look.
What they see stays in step with what they hear.
And in a video, every new idea means a fresh picture on screen.

scenes.narration: It's a default, not a law. Break it for comparisons, summaries, reference slides and process diagrams, where seeing several things together is the whole point.

slide.title: When to break the rule
slide.text: Comparisons. Summaries and agendas. Reference slides. Process diagrams
slide.notes: It's a default, not a law. Break it for comparisons, summaries, reference slides and process diagrams, where seeing several things together is the whole point.

scenes.storyboard: paper-light scene for contrast. Four small slide-thumbnails appear in a 2x2 grid, each drawn in line art: two columns for comparisons, a short list for summaries, a table for reference, a five-step flow for process. Each pops in on the word that names it with a coral underline sweep.

beats.text: It's a default, not a law.
Break it for comparisons, summaries, reference slides and process diagrams, where seeing several things together is the whole point.

scenes.narration: Builds let a fuller slide show several items without overwhelming anyone. Each point arrives as you talk about it.

slide.title: Reveal one point at a time
slide.text: Builds show several items. Reveal each as you talk about it
slide.notes: Builds let a fuller slide show several items without overwhelming anyone. Each point arrives as you talk about it.

scenes.storyboard: one fuller slide with four elements. Each element slides in on its own beat while earlier ones dim slightly and the newest glows with a violet ring, so there is always exactly one thing in focus. A thin timeline dot tracks along the bottom.

beats.text: Builds let a fuller slide show several items without overwhelming anyone.
Each point arrives as you talk about it.
